newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BCN, Alliance Capital form venture.
newsitem.headline: BCN, Alliance Capital form venture.

text.p: Brazil's BCN and U.S.-based Alliance Capital Management LP on Tuesday said they have formed an equally-owned joint-venture to provide asset management services in Brazil and, in a second stage, in Argentina.
BCN Alliance Capital Management will begin administering 1.4 billion reais, of which 1.1 billion reais in mutual funds and assets already managed by BCN.
"The venture will begin administering the 11 mutual funds under BCN management," BCN President Pedro Conde told a news conference to announce the deal.
The remainder are Brazilian assets under Alliance management.
The venture will offer asset and investment management services to foreign and domestic individuals and institutional investors.
Alliance Capital President John Carifa said the venture is part of the company's strategy to become the premier global investment management organization in the world.
"To reach that objective, we open offices and create ventures," he said. "We are very much committed to make that venture (with BCN) work."

Alliance Capital, which manages about $200 billion in assets, has 17 offices outside the U.S. and partnerships in Poland, Austria, India, Japan and Hong Kong. The company manages $23 billion to $25 billion outside the U.S.
Carifa said Brazil's fund industry has a great growth potential as the country's economic stability allows Brazilians to seek long-term investment and increase their savings.
"Mutual and pension funds have been growing significantly in Brazil and we expect this (growth) to accelerate," he said.

Brazilian fund assets currently total $125 billion, of which $75 billion are pension fund assets, BCN Alliance said. Those funds together represent 17 percent of Brazil's gross domestic product and virtually 90 percent are allocated in fixed income investments, it added.

Since 1990, the fund industry has been growing 50 percent annually, with pension funds growing 21 percent a year from 1983 and 1996, it said. "That shows the market's potential," said Roberto Correa da Fonseca, president of the new company.

Alliance is the latest asset manager to enter the Brazilian market. More recently, Prudential Securities, the fourth largest U.S. brokerage house, and Fidelity Investments, the world's largest mutual fund manager, opened their own offices in Brazil.
Fonseca said BCN Alliance expects to consolidate its business in Brazil in a few months, allowing it to think about its entry in Argentina.

He also said it is difficult to predict how far the venture can grow, but noted it expects to snap up a 2.5 percent stake in the Brazilian fund industry, the same market share that BCN has among local commercial banks, in a few years.
BCN is Brazil's sixth largest private bank, with 14.06 billion reais in total assets and a 1.059 billion real net worth.
